title: Fair distinctions make not-all-equal worlds a percolation problem at exactly 1/2
subject: Why the global emergence of not-all-equal worlds on surfaces is scale-free on the square lattice
conclusion: Recoloured, fair visible distinctions orient the hidden implications of a not-all-equal world by coin flips, reach through them is bond percolation at exactly 1/2, and a world without a directed crossing of its cut torus in one direction is consistent. So global emergence vanishes below a lattice's bond threshold, stays bounded on the square lattice, where self-duality puts the threshold at 1/2, and diverges when two-way contacts percolate.
